data.title: Disclosure-Gated User Simulation for Companion-Agent Evaluation
data.description: arXiv:2609.00982v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Playing the user with a large language model is standard in scalable evaluation, and has a repeatedly diagnosed failure: the simulated user is excessively cooperative, so a system under test can score by the number of questions it asks rather than by making the user willing to speak. We answer with a disclosure gate conditioning information release on the companion agent's behaviour: its state is a ladder of five ordered gates, merged onto three observable depth layers. We specify, ablate, and audit it. The gate is a load-bearing component of the environment: on a published companion-agent benchmark's English corpus, withdrawing per-example gate statements from training displaces the ranking of the 12 systems beyond the noise band of a seed re-run, while per-system scores show no detectable change. We state two acceptance criteria: a ranking must be order-preserving, and absolute scores must be scale-stable. Only one candidate passes both -- the simulator we release -- correlating at 0.993 with the published leaderboard. Prompting a frontier model instead barely moves the ranking while shifting every score up, invisible to ranking-only checks; we supply the specification, ablations, and downstream sensitivity analysis the benchmark's environment lacked.
data.author: Yao Liu, Yu He, Jihao Huang, Xinyang Liu, Feng Zhou
